title: Times New Roman and Arial 12-point versus 10-point legibility
statement:
In a controlled computer-display study of Times New Roman and Arial, 12-point text was perceived as more legible than 10-point text, while objective accuracy differences were small, so web interfaces have evidence for choosing 12pt over 10pt when readability matters more than maximum density.

Options:
- Dense: 10pt (fits: high density, technical)
- Readability baseline: 12pt (fits: balanced, professional)
- More comfortable: 14pt (fits: comfortable, friendly)
- Large reading: 16pt (fits: editorial, access-first)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web, web apps, content sites. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: Comparing the Effects of Text Size and Format on the Readability of Computer-Displayed Times New Roman and Arial Text
source.authors: Michael L. Bernard; Barbara S. Chaparro; Melissa M. Mills; Charles G. Halcomb
